new_note: *And there will be great wrath from Yahuah (God) against the children of Yashar’el (Israel), because they have forsaken His covenant and turned aside from His word, and provoked and blasphemed, inasmuch as they do not observe the ordinance of this law; for they have treated their members like the nations, so that they may be removed and rooted out of the land. And there will no more be pardon or forgiveness to them so that there should be forgiveness and pardon for all the sin of this eternal error.* (Jubilees 15:34). *Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.* (Matthew 12:31). Jubilees says a thing most readers do not expect from the book of the covenant: there is a sin for which there will no more be pardon. It is not a slip or a weakness. It is the children of Yashar'el (Israel) knowing the ordinance, forsaking the covenant on purpose, and treating the sign in their own flesh the way the nations do. Yahusha (Jesus) draws the same line in Matthew: every manner of sin and blasphemy can be forgiven, but the one who has watched the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) at work and called it something else has stepped past the place where forgiveness reaches. Both texts describe the same posture, a deliberate turning aside from what one has plainly seen, and both say the same thing about where it ends.
member_note: Jubilees 15:34 — *there will no more be pardon or forgiveness to them.* The deliberate forsaking of the covenant and the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) at Matthew 12:31 end in the same place, past forgiveness.

new_note: *And do you write down for yourself all these words which I declare to you on this mountain, the first and the last, which shall come to pass in all the divisions of the days in the law and in the testimony and in the weeks and the jubilees to eternity, until I descend and dwell with them throughout eternity."* (Jubilees 1:26). *Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.* (Psalm 139:16). Moses is told to write down the first and the last, everything that will come to pass in all the divisions of the days, before any of those days have arrived. David says the same thing about his own body: every member written in the book of Yahuah (God) while there was not yet one of them. In both the writing comes first and the days come after. The history of Yashar'el (Israel) laid out on Sinai in weeks and jubilees is not a forecast; it is a reading from a book already written, the same book David saw his unformed self in.
member_note: Jubilees 1:26 — *the first and the last, which shall come to pass in all the divisions of the days.* Written before it happens, as David's members were written in the book before there was one of them (Psalm 139:16).

new_note: *And he saw in a vision of the night, and behold an angel descended from heaven with seven tablets in his hands, and he gave them to Jacob, and he read them and knew all that was written therein which would befall him and his sons through- out all the ages.* (Jubilees 32:21). *Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.* (Psalm 139:16). Jacob is handed seven tablets and reads on them everything that will befall him and his sons through all the ages, and he reads it as settled, not as possibility. David had seen the same kind of writing: his members written in the book of Yahuah (God) when as yet there was none of them. The tablets Jacob read and the book David speaks of are the same heavenly writing, where the days are set down before they are lived. What came to Jacob's sons over the ages had already been read by their father at Bethel.
member_note: Jubilees 32:21 — *an angel descended from heaven with seven tablets in his hands, and he gave them to Jacob.* Jacob read what would befall his sons through all the ages, already written, as David's days were written before they came (Psalm 139:16).

new_note: *And he clothed him with byssus garments, and he put a gold chain upon his neck, and (a herald) proclaimed before him “’Êl ’Êl wa’ Abîrĕr,” and he placed a ring on his hand and made him ruler over all his house, and magnified him, and said to him: “Only on the throne shall I be greater than you.”* (Jubilees 40:7). *He made him lord of his house, and ruler of all his substance:* (Psalm 105:21). Pharaoh does the clothing, the chain, the ring, and the speaking, and Jubilees records every piece of it; the herald even cries before Joseph as he passes. The psalm names none of that. It says *He made him lord of his house*, and the He of Psalm 105 is Yahuah (God), whom the psalm has been praising from its first line. Jubilees shows the hand of the king setting Joseph over all his house; the psalm shows whose hand moved the king. The ruler of all Egypt was made ruler by the one who had been with him in the pit and the prison.
member_note: Jubilees 40:7 — *made him ruler over all his house, and magnified him.* Pharaoh did the clothing and the speaking, but Psalm 105:21 says who made Joseph lord: *He made him lord of his house*, and the He is Yahuah (God).

new_note: *And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.* (Jubilees 46:1). *When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt:* (Matthew 2:14). Jubilees opens its account of Egypt with a people at rest there. After Jacob died the children of Yashar'el (Israel) multiplied, became a great nation, and loved one another all the days of Joseph; Egypt was a shelter before it was a prison. Matthew's Joseph takes the child down the same road by night, and Egypt shelters him too, until Herod is dead. The child walks the path his people walked, a sojourn in Egypt and a calling out of it, so that what happened to the nation happens again in the one who came for the nation.
member_note: Jubilees 46:1 — *the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation.* Egypt sheltered the nation under one Joseph and the child under another (Matthew 2:14).

new_note: *And I have chosen the seed of Jacob from amongst all that I have seen, and have written him down as My firstborn son, and have sanctified him to Myself for ever and ever; and I will teach them the Sabbath day, that they may keep Sabbath thereon from all work.”* (Jubilees 2:20). *And was there until the death of Herod: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of Yahuah (Lord) by the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt have I called my son.* (Matthew 2:15). On the day the Sabbath is made, before Abraham, before Egypt, Yahuah (God) says He has chosen the seed of Jacob and written him down as His firstborn son. That writing is older than every event that follows it. When Matthew quotes the prophet, *Out of Egypt have I called my son*, the son in the prophet's mouth is the firstborn son named here at creation, the seed of Jacob brought up out of Egypt. Matthew says the child in Egypt fulfilled that word. The one who came for the firstborn walked the firstborn's road, and *my son* was written over the people before it was spoken over the child.
member_note: Jubilees 2:20 — *have written him down as My firstborn son, and have sanctified him to Myself for ever and ever.* The son called out of Egypt (Matthew 2:15) is the firstborn son written down at creation.

new_note: *And Rachel died there and she was buried in the land of Ephrath, the same is Bethlehem, and Jacob built a pillar on the grave of Rachel, on the road above her grave.* (Jubilees 32:34). *In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.* (Matthew 2:18). Jubilees places Rachel's grave where Genesis does, in the land of Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, with Jacob's pillar on the road above it. That is the road Herod's soldiers came down. Matthew reaches for Jeremiah's picture of Rachel weeping for her children because the mother of Joseph and Benjamin lies at the door of the town where the children were killed. The weeping is not a figure chosen at random; it is the voice of the one buried there, and the children slain at Bethlehem fell within sight of her pillar.
member_note: Jubilees 32:34 — *she was buried in the land of Ephrath, the same is Bethlehem.* Rachel weeps at Matthew 2:18 from a grave on the Bethlehem road.

new_note: *And the chief of the spirits, Mastêmâ, came and said: “Yahuah (God), Creator, let some of them remain before me, and let them hearken to my voice, and do all that I shall say to them; for if some of them are not left to me, I shall not be able to execute the power of my will on the sons of men; for these are for corruption and leading astray before my judgment, for great is the wickedness of the sons of men.”* (Jubilees 10:8). *Then was Yahusha (Jesus) led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.* (Matthew 4:1). Mastema does not seize his place; he asks for it. He stands before Yahuah (God) and asks that some of the spirits be left to him so that he can lead the sons of men astray before the judgment, and the answer is *Let the tenth part of them remain before him* (Jubilees 10:9). So when Matthew says Yahusha (Jesus) was led up of the Spirit to be tempted of the devil, the tempter is not an intruder working outside the will of Yahuah (God). He is the one who asked for room to test the sons of men and was given it. The Spirit led the Son of Adam straight into that permitted testing, and he came out of it whole.
member_note: Jubilees 10:8 — *let some of them remain before me, and let them hearken to my voice.* The devil who tempted Yahusha (Jesus) in the wilderness (Matthew 4:1) works inside a permission he asked for.

new_note: *And the prince Mastêmâ sent ravens and birds to devour the seed which was sown in the land, in order to destroy the land, and rob the children of men of their labours. Before they could plough in the seed, the ravens picked (it) from the surface of the ground.* (Jubilees 11:11). *And when the tempter came to him, he said, If thou be the Son of Elohim (God), command that these stones be made bread.* (Matthew 4:3). Before Abraham was born, Mastema was already at war with bread. He sent the ravens to take the seed off the ground before it could be ploughed in, so that men's labour fed nothing and the land went hungry, and Terah's name carries the memory of it. In the wilderness the tempter comes to a hungry man with the same subject. He does not offer Yahusha (Jesus) a kingdom first; he offers bread, and tells him to make it himself rather than wait on the Father who feeds. The one who stole the bread from Terah's fields is the one who held it out in the wilderness, and he was refused.
member_note: Jubilees 11:11 — *the prince Mastêmâ sent ravens and birds to devour the seed which was sown in the land.* The enemy who stole the bread from the fields is the tempter who held out bread in the wilderness (Matthew 4:3).

new_note: *And the prince Mastêmâ came and said before Elohim (God), “Behold, Abraham loves Isaac his son, and he delights in him above all things else; bid him offer him as a burnt-offering on the altar, and You will see if he will do this command, and You will know if he is faithful in everything wherein You do try him.”* (Jubilees 17:16). *Then the devil taketh him up into the holy city, and setteth him on a pinnacle of the temple,* (Matthew 4:5). Jubilees lets the reader hear what Genesis leaves silent: the testing of Abraham began with Mastema standing before Elohim (God) and asking for it. His argument is that love must be proven by a command obeyed, and he names the dearest thing. The devil on the pinnacle makes the same move, pressing the Son to prove his sonship by a visible act. Abraham was tested with Isaac; Yahusha (Jesus) was tested with himself. In both the accuser proposed the trial, Yahuah (God) allowed it, and the faithful one came through it without giving the accuser what he asked for.
member_note: Jubilees 17:16 — *bid him offer him as a burnt-offering on the altar, and You will see if he will do this command.* The accuser who proposed Abraham's trial proposes the Son's on the pinnacle (Matthew 4:5).

new_note: *And He made for all His works a new and righteous nature, so that they should not sin in their whole nature for ever, but should be all righteous each in his kind alway.* (Jubilees 5:12). *Destroy all wrong from the face of the earth and let every evil work come to an end: and let the plant of righteousness and truth appear: and it shall prove a blessing; the works of righteousness and truth shall be planted in truth and joy for evermore.* (1 Enoch 10:16). After the flood Yahuah (God) did not only wash the earth; He made for all His works a new and righteous nature, so that each kind should be righteous in its kind. Enoch heard the same thing commanded before it was done: destroy all wrong, let every evil work end, and let the plant of righteousness and truth appear. The plant Enoch was shown is the nature Jubilees says was made. Judgment in both books is not the end of the story but the clearing of the ground for what is planted in truth and joy for evermore.
member_note: Jubilees 5:12 — *He made for all His works a new and righteous nature.* The plant of righteousness and truth of 1 Enoch 10:16 is this new nature made after the flood.

new_note: *For Yahuah (God) has four places on the earth, the Garden of Eden, and the Mount of the East, and this mountain on which you are this day, Mount Sinai, and Mount Zion (which) will be sanctified in the new creation for a sanctification of the earth; through it will the earth be sanctified from all (its) guilt and its uncleanness throughout the generations of the world.* (Jubilees 4:26). *And he answered saying: ‘This high mountain which thou hast seen, whose summit is like the throne of Elohim (God), is His throne, where the Holy Great One, Yahuah (Lord) of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.* (1 Enoch 25:3). Jubilees counts four places of Yahuah (God) on the earth and says the last of them, Mount Zion, will be sanctified in the new creation and sanctify the earth through it. Enoch was shown a high mountain whose summit is like the throne of Elohim (God), where the Eternal King will sit when He comes down to visit the earth with goodness. The two books are looking at the same thing from two sides, a mountain on this earth that becomes the seat of His coming. Jubilees names it among the holy places; Enoch sees Him sitting on it. The sanctifying of the earth and the visiting of the earth with goodness are one descent.
member_note: Jubilees 4:26 — *Mount Zion (which) will be sanctified in the new creation for a sanctification of the earth.* The mountain of 1 Enoch 25:3, whose summit is His throne, stands among the four holy places of the earth.

new_note: *And Pharaoh gave back Sarai, the wife of Abram, and he sent him out of the land of Egypt, and he journeyed to the place where he had pitched his tent at the beginning, to the place of the altar, with Ai on the east, and Bethel on the west, and he blessed Yahuah (God) his Elohim (God) who had brought him back in peace. And it came to pass in the forty-first jubilee, in the third year of the first week, that he returned to this place and offered thereon a burnt sacrifice, and called on the name of Yahuah (God), and said: “You, the most high Elohim (God), are my Elohim (God) for ever and ever.”* (Jubilees 13:15–16). *Unto the place of the altar, which he had made there at the first: and there Abram called on the name of Yahuah (LORD).* (Genesis 13:4). Genesis gives the return in one line: back to the first altar, and there Abram called on the name of Yahuah (LORD). Jubilees fills in what the calling said. He blessed the one who had brought him back in peace, and then he called on the name and spoke to it: You, the most high Elohim (God), are my Elohim (God) for ever and ever. Calling on the name was never a bare invocation. It was a man coming back to the place where he had first built an altar and saying out loud, with the land and the altar as witnesses, whose he was and for how long.
member_note: Jubilees 13:15 — *he journeyed to the place where he had pitched his tent at the beginning, to the place of the altar.* The return of Genesis 13:4, with the words of the calling on the name given in the next verse.

new_note: *And he believed in Yahuah (God), and it was counted to him for righteousness. And He said to him: “I am Yahuah (God) that brought you out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give you the land of the Canaanites to possess it for ever; and I shall be Elohim (God) to you and to your seed after you.”* (Jubilees 14:6–7). *And he believed in Yahuah (LORD); and he counted it to him for righteousness.* (Genesis 15:6). Jubilees carries Genesis 15:6 almost word for word, and then does not let the reader walk away from it. In the next breath the one who counted the belief for righteousness says who He is: the one who brought Abram out of Ur, who gives the land to his seed, who will be Elohim (God) to him and to his seed after him. The reckoned righteousness is not a doorway out of the covenant; it is spoken inside it, with the land and the seed and the Elohim (God) of the seed all named in the same speech. Faith was counted and the covenant was declared, and neither was set against the other.
member_note: Jubilees 14:6 — *he believed in Yahuah (God), and it was counted to him for righteousness.* Genesis 15:6 word for word, spoken inside the covenant that names the land and the seed in the next breath.

new_note: *And Yahuah (God) opened seven flood-gates of heaven, And the mouths of the fountains of the great deep, seven mouths in number.* (Jubilees 5:24). *And I saw again, and behold fountains were opened on the surface of that great enclosure, and that water began to swell and rise upon the surface, and I saw that enclosure till all its surface was covered with water.* (1 Enoch 89:3). Jubilees counts the openings: seven flood-gates of heaven and seven mouths of the fountains of the great deep. Enoch saw the fountains from above, opened on the surface of the great enclosure, the water swelling and rising until the whole surface was covered. One book gives the number and the other gives the sight, and they are describing the same morning. The deep did not leak; it was opened, by mouths, on purpose, and both witnesses say so.
member_note: Jubilees 5:24 — *the mouths of the fountains of the great deep, seven mouths in number.* The fountains Enoch saw opened on the surface of the enclosure (1 Enoch 89:3).

new_note: *And lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way, alike men and cattle and beasts and birds and everything that walks on the earth-all of them corrupted their ways and their orders, and they began to devour each other, and lawlessness increased on the earth and every imagination of the thoughts of all men (was) thus evil continually.* (Jubilees 5:2). *Who consumed all the acquisitions of men.* (1 Enoch 7:3). Jubilees says all flesh corrupted its way and they began to devour each other, and leaves the devouring without a face. Enoch gives it one. The giants born to the angels' wives consumed all the acquisitions of men, everything men had laboured for, until there was nothing left to give them. The lawlessness that filled the earth before the flood was not only men sinning against men; it was the offspring of the fallen eating the world out from under the sons of Adam. Read together, the two books show that the flood came against a devouring that had a lineage, not merely a mood.
member_note: Jubilees 5:2 — *they began to devour each other.* The devouring has a face: the giants *Who consumed all the acquisitions of men* (1 Enoch 7:3).

new_note: *And Jacob vowed a vow to Yahuah (God), saying: “If Yahuah (God) will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and give me bread to eat and raiment to put on, so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, then shall Yahuah (God) be my Elohim (God), and this stone which I have set up as a pillar for a sign in this place, shall be Yahuah (God)’s house, and of all that you give me, I shall give the tenth to you, my Elohim (God).”* (Jubilees 27:27). *For he told them how he had seen everything in a dream, even all that He had spoken to him that he should return to his father’s house; and they said: “To every place whither you go we will go with you.”* (Jubilees 29:3). Jacob's vow at Bethel asks for one thing in particular: to come again to his father's house in peace. Years later, when he tells his wives why they are leaving Laban, what he tells them is a dream in which Yahuah (God) spoke to him that he should return to his father's house. The vow and the dream use the same words because the dream is the answer to the vow. Jubilees lets the reader see both ends of it: the stone set up as a pillar with a promise attached, and the command that sends him back to keep it.
member_note: Jubilees 27:27 — *so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, then shall Yahuah (God) be my Elohim (God).* The dream at Jubilees 29:3 that sends him back to his father's house answers this vow.

new_note: *And the king called Joseph’s name Sĕphânṭîphâns, and gave Joseph to wife the daughter of Potiphar, the daughter of the priest of Heliopolis, the chief cook.* (Jubilees 40:10). *And your name no more shall be called Joseph, but Zaphnath Paaneah shall be your name; you shall be second to me, and according to your word shall be all the affairs of my government, and at your word shall my people go out and come in.* (Jasher 49:21). The king gives Joseph a new name, and both books record it. Jubilees writes it as Sĕphânṭîphâns and Jasher writes it as Zaphnath Paaneah; it is one Egyptian name heard through two scribes' ears, the same name Genesis carries. Jasher adds what the name meant in Pharaoh's mouth: second to me, every affair of the government at your word, the people going out and coming in at your word. Jubilees adds the wife, the priest's daughter from Heliopolis. The two books do not compete; each keeps a piece of the same afternoon in Pharaoh's court.
member_note: Jubilees 40:10 — *the king called Joseph’s name Sĕphânṭîphâns.* The new name Jasher 49:21 gives as Zaphnath Paaneah.

new_note: *And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.* (Jubilees 46:14). *Behold in the land are Pithom and Rameses, cities unfortified against battle, it behooves you and us to build them, and to fortify them.* (Jasher 65:8). Jasher records the counsel that proposed the work: Pithom and Rameses stood unfortified against battle, and the Egyptians said it behooved them to build and fortify. Jubilees records the work itself: taskmasters set over the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and the strong cities Pithom and Raamses built for Pharaoh, with all the walls and fortifications that had fallen. The one book gives the plan and the other gives the labour, and the same two cities stand at the centre of both. The fortifying Jasher's counsellors called for is the fortification Jubilees says Yashar'el (Israel) raised with their own hands under the taskmasters.
member_note: Jubilees 46:14 — *they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses.* The same two cities the Egyptians resolved to fortify at Jasher 65:8.

new_note: *And he took fig-leaves and sewed (them) together, and made an apron for himself, and covered his shame. And Elohim (God) cursed the serpent, and was wroth with it for ever….* (Jubilees 3:22–23). *After this Satan called to his hosts, all of which came to him, and said to him:--* (1 Adam and Eve 48:1). Jubilees moves in two lines from Adam sewing fig-leaves to the serpent cursed for ever. The First Book of Adam and Eve picks the story up outside the garden, where the same serpent, now named Satan, calls his hosts together to plan against the man he has already brought down. The curse did not end his hostility; it fixed it. The one Elohim (God) was wroth with for ever is the one still gathering his hosts against the sons of Adam, and the later book shows the war continuing where Genesis and Jubilees fall silent.
member_note: Jubilees 3:22 — *he took fig-leaves and sewed (them) together, and made an apron for himself, and covered his shame.* The serpent cursed in the next line is the Satan who calls his hosts against the man at 1 Adam and Eve 48:1.
flag: 1 Adam and Eve 48:1 as given is only the lead-in line ('After this Satan called to his hosts... and said to him:--'); the note leans on it as the rallying of the hosts, which is all the verse carries.

new_note: *And he built there an altar to Yahuah (God) who had delivered him, and who was making him rejoice in the land of his sojourning, and he celebrated a festival of joy in this month seven days, near the altar which he had built at the Well of the Oath. And he built booths for himself and for his servants on this festival, and he was the first to celebrate the feast of tabernacles on the earth.* (Jubilees 16:20–21). *And Abraham planted a grove in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of Yahuah (LORD), El Olam (the everlasting God).* (Genesis 21:33). Genesis says Abraham planted a grove at Beer-sheba and called there on the name of Yahuah (LORD), El Olam (the everlasting God). Beer-sheba is the Well of the Oath, and Jubilees tells what the calling looked like there: an altar built to the one who had delivered him, seven days of a festival of joy beside it, booths for himself and his servants, and the first feast of tabernacles ever kept on the earth. The grove and the altar and the name all belong to one appointed time. Abraham called on the everlasting name by keeping the feast, long before Sinai wrote the feast down.
member_note: Jubilees 16:20 — *he celebrated a festival of joy in this month seven days.* The calling on the name at Beer-sheba (Genesis 21:33) was the first feast of tabernacles on the earth.

new_note: *I shall give to your seed all the earth which is under heaven, and they will judge all the nations according to their desires, and after that they will get possession of the whole earth and inherit it for ever.”* (Jubilees 32:19). *And the land which I gave Abraham and Isaac, to thee I will give it, and to thy seed after thee will I give the land.* (Genesis 35:12). At Bethel the promise to Jacob in Genesis is the land, the land given to Abraham and Isaac, now given to him and to his seed after him. Jubilees records the same promise at the same place and lets it run to its full length: all the earth which is under heaven, the nations judged by his seed, and the whole earth possessed and inherited for ever. The land promised to the fathers was never the ceiling. It was the first instalment of an inheritance that widens to the whole earth, held by the seed of Jacob gathered home, and both books are describing the one promise at its two ends.
member_note: Jubilees 32:19 — *they will get possession of the whole earth and inherit it for ever.* The land of Genesis 35:12 widened to the whole earth for Jacob's seed.
flag: Live 32:19 opens with the misprint 'Ana I shall give'; the quote starts at 'I shall give' so it is a verbatim substring but not the full verse.

new_note: *And Yahuah (God) opened seven flood-gates of heaven, And the mouths of the fountains of the great deep, seven mouths in number. And the flood-gates began to pour down water from the heaven forty days and forty nights, And the fountains of the deep also sent up waters, until the whole world was full of water.* (Jubilees 5:24–25). *Whereby the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished:* (2 Peter 3:6). Peter says the scoffers of the last days willingly forget one thing: that the world that then was perished, overflowed with water. Jubilees does not let it be forgotten. It counts the flood-gates and the mouths of the deep, forty days and forty nights, until the whole world was full of water. The same picture Genesis gives stands here in the restored library with the numbers attached. The judgment the scoffers deny is written in more than one book, and it is not new.
member_note: Jubilees 5:24 — *opened seven flood-gates of heaven, And the mouths of the fountains of the great deep.* The world Peter says *being overflowed with water, perished* (2 Peter 3:6).
